samples.evidence: Project cloudtrail-detector. detect.py (412 lines): 3 heuristic rules over CloudTrail events (console-login-without-MFA burst, IAM policy attach outside change window, S3 public-acl change), thresholds in config.yaml. tests/ has 11 pytest cases with positive and negative fixtures; all passing per run log 2026-09-30. Fixture data in sample_data/ is labeled SYNTHETIC in the README. README also documents blind spots: no VPC flow logs, no DNS query visibility, single-account only.
samples.reference_rationale: Runnable detection logic with tunable thresholds, tests, and explicit blind spots = L2; synthetic fixtures force the (synthetic) scope suffix (rubric rule 3).

samples.evidence: analysis/walkthrough-014.md (236 lines): full phishing analysis done independently — header chain read, SPF/DKIM/DMARC results interpreted, landing URL decoded from the redirect wrapper, payload hash extracted and listed as IOC, final verdict 'malicious, high confidence' with the evidence weighted step by step. Dataset note on page 1: 'specimen reconstructed from a public phish corpus; not a live mailbox catch.'
samples.reference_rationale: Complete independent analysis loop with evidence-weighted verdict = L2; reconstructed specimen forces the (reconstructed) suffix.

samples.evidence: sigma-lite: a Python CLI that converts a folder of Sigma-style YAML rules to grep-able JSON queries. argparse CLI with --input/--output/--strict, clean error messages on malformed rules, 14 unit tests all passing (CI log in repo), README gives exact reproduce commands. Author wrote it to replace a manual copy-paste step in their log-review workflow and says so in the README.
samples.reference_rationale: Independent tool solving a real pain point, CLI + error handling + tests + reproducible README = L2. D7 grades code craft, so no scope suffix (rule 3 exception).

samples.evidence: agent-audit/ in a home-lab environment: inventory.md lists 3 deployed agents with identity, owner, model, and every granted tool (one agent held an unneeded file-write tool). audit-findings.md reviews two weeks of tool-call logs with excerpts: flags 14 unplanned file writes by that agent, traces them to an over-broad default profile, records remediation — token revoked, tool scope cut to read-only, re-test passed. Evaluator for the re-test was a different person than the agent's operator; both names recorded.
samples.reference_rationale: End-to-end log audit with evidence, least-privilege fix, credential revocation, and operator/evaluator separation = L2 for D8; lab environment forces the (lab) suffix.

samples.evidence: incident-reports/IR-2026-004.md is a polished 12-section incident report: executive summary, timeline with minute precision, 'root cause determined', containment described as complete. Cross-check: the timeline entries match the 'expected findings' list in attack-runbook.md word for word; the repo has no run records, no screenshots, no log excerpts, and the report's 'evidence' section links to files that do not exist.
samples.reference_rationale: Looks like a finished IR loop but the content is expected findings, not observed ones (rule 7), and the underlying artifact is a filled-in template with no run evidence (rule 6). Beyond a bare template (structure and lifecycle are understood) = L1+, not L2.

samples.evidence: README headline: 'Complete SOC monitoring suite — 40+ alerts triaged with full escalation chain.' Repo contents: triage-guide.md (well-written: receive → prioritize → assess → contain/escalate flow, four-tier severity model, 3 sample alerts worked from the guide's own examples with correct verdicts) and the README. No alert queue exports, no triage records, no playbook beyond the guide itself.
samples.reference_rationale: The guide work is strong L1 material and the worked samples push past plain L1, but describing and demonstrating on guide examples is not independently running the alert chain (compare rubric §6). Claim of 40 triaged alerts is unsupported. L1+.

samples.evidence: README headline: 'Automated malware triage platform.' Repo: notes.md accurately explains packing, section entropy, and sensitive API indicators; hashcheck.py (43 lines) prints a file's SHA-256 and average entropy and nothing else — no scoring, no thresholds, no tests, no sample run output. Author's summary calls the entropy printout 'behavioral verdict: suspicious'.
samples.reference_rationale: Solid indicator knowledge (L1) plus a minimal runnable script keeps it above bare L1, but there is no triage tool in the rubric's sense — no scoring logic, no tests — and an entropy number is not a verdict. L1+, not L2.

samples.evidence: README headline: 'Production-grade AWS security monitoring, deployed.' Repo: architecture.md gives a correct, clear explanation of what CloudTrail, GuardDuty, and Security Hub each do and where their coverage overlaps; main.tf defines a plausible logging stack. No terraform state, no apply logs, no detection findings, no screenshots of a running environment — nothing shows the stack was ever deployed or an alert ever fired.
samples.reference_rationale: Explaining the services well is L1; a complete, credible IaC definition pushes to L1+. L2 requires a built environment with observed detections — none are evidenced. 'Deployed' is a claim, not evidence.

samples.evidence: triage-notes.md (student's own file): the alert flow written in their own words in 5 lines; a severity table (copied from a public guide, credited); two sample alerts with one-line verdicts that match the guide's published answer key. Nothing worked independently.
samples.reference_rationale: Describes the flow, uses a severity model, works sample alerts from a guide — the definition of D1 L1. No independent chain, so nothing higher.

samples.evidence: Repo 'log-analyzer': README says 'coming soon — will parse CloudTrail and flag bad events.' Only code file is grepwrap.py (15 lines), which fails with a SyntaxError as committed (run output pasted in issues). No log fields discussed anywhere, no sample queries, no data.
samples.reference_rationale: No creditable evidence: cannot read log fields, no retrieval demonstrated, the only code does not run. Not covered = none.

samples.evidence: email-auth-notes.md: accurate short explanations of SPF, DKIM, and DMARC and what 'alignment' means, following a cheatsheet; one raw header block pasted with the From/Return-Path fields underlined. No analysis of any message beyond that, no verdicts.
samples.reference_rationale: Reads key header fields and explains the auth protocols from a cheatsheet = D4 L1 exactly. No independent analysis performed.

samples.evidence: Slide deck 'AI Governance Framework v1' (9 slides): buzzword diagrams ('human-in-the-loop', 'guardrails', 'trust layer'), a maturity model copied in style from vendor blogs. No agent inventory, no tool or permission lists, no log excerpts, no evaluation records, no incident handling — nothing the author personally operated or audited.
samples.reference_rationale: D8 L1 already requires an agent inventory and reading real tool-call logs. A vocabulary deck evidences none of that. Not covered = none.
